scheme.value: HMAC-SHA256 (default algorithm, filterable via woocommerce_webhook_hash_algorithm), raw binary digest, then base64 encoded
scheme.quote: return base64_encode( hash_hmac( $hash_algo, $payload, wp_specialchars_decode( $this->get_secret(), ENT_QUOTES ), true ) );

scheme_doc_comment.value: The source comment describes it as a base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the payload body
scheme_doc_comment.quote: Generate a base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature of the payload body

hash_algorithm_filter.value: The algorithm defaults to sha256 but a site can change it with the woocommerce_webhook_hash_algorithm filter

signed_content.value: The exact request body string that is sent: trim( wp_json_encode( $payload ) ). The signature is generated from that already-encoded string (JSON by default).

signed_content_note.value: Source comment: the signature is calculated after the body has been encoded
signed_content_note.quote: is calculated after the body has already been encoded (JSON by default).

header_format.value: Bare base64 string, no prefix, no timestamp, one signature
header_format.quote: X-WC-Webhook-Signature - a base64 encoded HMAC-SHA256 hash of the payload.

secret_source.value: A secret set on the webhook in WooCommerce (Settings > Advanced > Webhooks > Secret field, or the REST API `secret` property). Left blank in the admin screen, the source generates a 50-character password. The woocommerce.com doc says a blank secret defaults to the current API user's consumer secret; see conflicts.
secret_source.quote: Secret — Enter a secret key used to generate a hash of the delivered webhook. The hash is included in the request headers.
secret_source.short: The webhook's Secret field (generated when left blank)

secret_default_in_admin_source.value: Admin screen: posted secret if given, otherwise wp_generate_password( 50, true, true )

secret_default_in_rest_source.value: REST create: request secret if given, otherwise wp_generate_password( 50, true, true )

secret_html_decoding.value: The secret is passed through wp_specialchars_decode( ..., ENT_QUOTES ) before it is used as the HMAC key, so a secret stored with HTML entities is decoded first

secret_scope.value: Per webhook (each webhook record has its own `secret`)
secret_scope.quote: Get the secret used for generating the HMAC-SHA256 signature.

secret_filter.value: The secret can be overridden by the woocommerce_webhook_secret filter at read time

timestamp_tolerance.value: not stated by the provider (the signature covers the body only; no timestamp header is sent)

rotation.value: not stated by the provider (updating the secret on the webhook replaces it; no dual signing is documented)

raw_body_note.value: The signature is over the exact encoded body string; no prose from the provider about raw body handling beyond the source comment

method_and_content_type.value: POST, Content-Type application/json, redirects not followed (redirection 0), request timeout 60 seconds

headers_x_wc_webhook_source.value: X-WC-Webhook-Source: the site's home URL with trailing slash (home_url( '/' ))

headers_x_wc_webhook_id.value: X-WC-Webhook-ID: the numeric ID of the webhook (not the delivery)

headers_x_wc_webhook_delivery_id.value: X-WC-Webhook-Delivery-ID: a hash generated per delivery

event_type_location.value: Headers X-WC-Webhook-Topic (resource.event, e.g. order.updated), X-WC-Webhook-Resource and X-WC-Webhook-Event. The JSON body does not carry the topic.

delivery_id.value: X-WC-Webhook-Delivery-ID header. The source builds it as wp_hash( webhook_id . strtotime( 'now' ) ), a hash of the webhook ID and the current time in whole seconds.

delivery_id_comment.value: Source comment on how the ID is generated
delivery_id_comment.quote: we generate a unique hash instead based on current time and webhook ID.

payload.value: JSON; for the API resources (coupons, customers, orders, products) the body is the same as the REST API response for that resource. Custom `action.*` topics pass the first hook argument.
payload.quote: the response is exactly the same as if requested via the REST API.

handshake.value: A ping is sent to the delivery URL when a webhook is first created / first saved as Active: a POST whose body is the string `webhook_id=<id>` (form-style, not JSON). The ping args set only user-agent and body in the source (no Content-Type, no X-WC-Webhook-* headers, no signature). The ping must be answered with exactly 200.
handshake.short: Unsigned ping, body webhook_id=<id>, on activation; answer 200

ping_when.value: Sent when a webhook is first created and when it is first activated
ping_when.quote: Send a test ping to the delivery URL, sent when the webhook is first created.

ping_when_doc.value: The first time a webhook is saved with Active status
ping_when_doc.quote: The first time you save a webhook with the Active status, WooCommerce sends a ping to the Delivery URL.

ping_success.value: Only HTTP 200 counts for the ping; any other code or an unreachable URL returns an error to the admin screen

ping_in_rest.value: Creating a webhook through the REST API also sends a ping

batching.value: One event per request (one payload built from one hook argument per delivery)

async_delivery.value: Delivery is queued at the end of the request (shutdown hook) and by default run in the background through WooCommerce's queue as the woocommerce_deliver_webhook_async action in group woocommerce-webhooks; woocommerce_webhook_deliver_async can force immediate delivery
async_delivery.quote: Webhooks are processed in the background by default

queue_backend.value: WC()->queue()->add is implemented with Action Scheduler (as_schedule_single_action)

coalescing_window.value: The same webhook with the same hook arguments is scheduled at most once per 10 minutes (an already-pending action is not duplicated)
coalescing_window.quote: only schedule one webhook every 10 minutes to maintain backward compatibility with WP Cron behaviour seen in WC < 3.5.0.

rest_doc_async_statement.value: The REST docs say delivery is processed in the background using wp-cron (see conflicts)
rest_doc_async_statement.quote: processed in the background by default using wp-cron.

success_status.value: Any 2xx, plus 301 and 302 (the doc wording). The source condition counts any code from 200 up to and including 302 as success; redirects are not followed.
success_status.quote: A failure is any response that is not a 2xx, 301, or 302 HTTP status code.

success_status_source.value: Code: response >= 200 and < 303 resets the failure counter

response_deadline.value: 60 seconds (HTTP timeout set to MINUTE_IN_SECONDS); not documented in prose

redirects.value: Redirects are not followed (a 301/302 is read as the response and counted as success)

retries.value: not stated by the provider. The source performs one wp_safe_remote_request per scheduled delivery and I found no retry logic in class-wc-webhook.php or wc-webhook-functions.php; a failed delivery only increments the consecutive-failure counter.
retries.short: None in the source; disabled after more than five consecutive failures

disabling.value: Webhook status becomes `disabled` after more than five consecutive failed deliveries (doc wording); threshold filter is woocommerce_max_webhook_delivery_failures (default 5); action hook woocommerce_webhook_disabled_due_delivery_failures fires. A re-enable requires editing the webhook (status back to Active).
disabling.quote: WooCommerce automatically disables a webhook after more than five consecutive delivery failures.

disabling_filter.quote: you can use the woocommerce_max_webhook_delivery_failures filter.

disabling_source.value: Source condition is `$failures > <filter, default 5>` evaluated before the counter is incremented; when true the status is set to disabled. (Reading of the code, not provider prose: the counter reaches 6 on the sixth consecutive failure and the webhook is disabled when the seventh consecutive failed delivery is processed.)

disabling_failure_definition_source_comm.value: Source comment defines the rule as more than 5 consecutive failures
disabling_failure_definition_source_comm.quote: if more than 5 consecutive failures occur.

status_values.value: active (delivers), paused (paused by admin), disabled (paused automatically due to consecutive failures)
status_values.quote: 'disabled' - does not delivery payload, paused automatically due to consecutive failures.

ordering.value: not stated by the provider (deliveries are independent background actions)

duplicates.value: not stated by the provider. Source suppresses re-processing of the same hook argument within one request and coalesces identical pending deliveries (see coalescing_window).

topics_core_doc.value: Core topics: coupon.created/updated/deleted, customer.created/updated/deleted, order.created/updated/deleted, product.created/updated/deleted (docs); plus action.<hook> custom topics

topics_source_events.value: Source accepts resources coupon, customer, order, product with events created, updated, deleted, restored, published, but only pairs that have a registered hook are valid (e.g. order.published and customer.restored are rejected)

topics_invalid_pairs.value: Default pairs with no registered hook are rejected

common.meaning: A new order was created (hook woocommerce_new_order)
Order updated; also fires on order refunds and refund deletion
Custom topic that fires when a WooCommerce action runs; names must start with action.woocommerce_ or action.wc_
common.quote: you can create a webhook that fires every time a product is added to the shopping cart by using the action woocommerce_add_to_cart

where_url_is_entered.value: WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Webhooks > Add webhook (Delivery URL field), or POST /wp-json/wc/v3/webhooks
where_url_is_entered.quote: Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Webhooks.

fields.value: Name, Status (Active / Paused / Disabled), Topic, Custom Topic, Action Event, Delivery URL, Secret
fields.quote: Delivery URL — Enter the URL where the webhook payload is delivered.

delivery_url_schemes.value: Delivery URL must be HTTP or HTTPS
delivery_url_schemes.quote: URL where the payload is delivered, must be HTTP or HTTPS.

test_tools.value: The ping on first activation; delivery logs under WooCommerce > Status > Logs (source webhooks-delivery) recording request duration, URL, headers, body and the response. No send-test-event or redelivery button is documented.
test_tools.quote: select webhooks-delivery from the All sources dropdown to filter the list.

delivery_logging.value: Request and response are logged; the body is only logged in WP_DEBUG mode
delivery_logging.quote: Webhook body is not logged unless WP_DEBUG mode is turned on.

ip_allowlist.value: not stated by the provider (webhooks are sent from the merchant's own site; X-WC-Webhook-Source names that site)

gotchas.value: The ping body is the plain string webhook_id=<id>, not JSON, and is not signed; a receiver that JSON-parses or verifies signatures on every POST will reject it, and the ping must return exactly 200 or the admin save reports an error
gotchas.quote: return new WP_Error( 'error', sprintf( __( 'Error: Delivery URL returned response code: %s', 'woocommerce' ), absint( $response_code ) ) );

gotchas.value: Failures are consecutive failed deliveries; any success resets the counter, and a webhook disabled by failures must be re-enabled by editing it
gotchas.quote: the webhook is disabled and must be edited via the REST API to re-enable.
For example, 4xx or 5xx responses count as failures.

gotchas.value: Payload for API resources mirrors the REST API response, so shapes follow the REST API version configured on the webhook
gotchas.quote: the response is exactly the same as if requested via the REST API.

gotchas.value: Identical pending deliveries are coalesced within 10 minutes, so rapid repeated updates of the same record may produce fewer webhooks than changes
gotchas.quote: Make webhooks unique - only schedule one webhook every 10 minutes

gotchas.value: Webhooks are delivered in the background so delivery lag depends on the site's queue runner (Action Scheduler), not on the triggering request
gotchas.quote: Webhooks are processed in the background by default

conflicts.note: Default secret when left blank (woocommerce.com doc vs source)

sources.quote: If you leave this blank, it defaults to the current API user’s consumer secret.

conflicts.topic: Default secret in the REST API (REST docs vs source)
conflicts.note: Default secret in the REST API (REST docs vs source)

sources.quote: This will default is a MD5 hash from the current user's ID|username if not provided.

conflicts.note: Background delivery mechanism (REST docs say wp-cron, source uses Action Scheduler)

sources.quote: processed in the background by default using wp-cron.

conflicts.note: Failure threshold wording (REST docs: after 5; woocommerce.com doc and source: more than 5)

conflicts.topic: Delivery ID (REST docs say a comment ID; source generates a hash)
conflicts.note: Delivery ID (REST docs say a comment ID; source generates a hash)

sources.quote: Since we no longer use comments to store delivery logs

conflicts.topic: Success status codes (REST docs: 2xx; woocommerce.com doc and source: also 301/302)
conflicts.note: Success status codes (REST docs: 2xx; woocommerce.com doc and source: also 301/302)
